results.fact: Which traverse the North Chute line crosses
results.correct_value: The North Chute tops out where the South Chute's gully joins; the shared line then crosses the Finger Traverse (usual ascent line), with the Terrible Traverse as the lower alternative
results.evidence: A 2013 trip report climbed the North Chute, crossed a left-trending ledge where the South Chute comes in, went through a notch and snowfield and then crossed the Finger Traverse, descending later by the Terrible Traverse. A separate 2013 party likewise ascended the North Chute, reached the Finger Traverse just above its top, and descended the South Chute via the Terrible Traverse. The route breakdown already matches this; the approach variants, watch_out, descent and itinerary said the chute commits you to the Terrible Traverse and are corrected.

patches.fact: Which traverse the North Chute line crosses
patches.find: THE CONFIRMING TEST IS ABOVE THE CHUTE, and it is what proves you took the right one: the North Chute leads toward the Terrible Traverse, the steep exposed snow crossing above a large cliff at roughly 7,435 ft. The South Chute leads to a notch at about 6,600 ft with the Cat Ears tower just left of it and then, after a saddle and a 150 ft descent and a second gully, to the Finger Traverse — a downsloping ledge with a horizontal finger crack and old pitons. If you top out and find a finger crack, you took the South Chute; if you top out and find a snow traverse over a cliff, you took this one.
patches.replace: THE CONFIRMING TEST IS AT THE TOP OF THE CHUTE: it narrows and eases, and the summit block comes into sight to the north for the first time. Just above, a narrow exposed ledge trending left meets the point where the South Chute's loose gully comes in from below. From there the two routes are the same line: north through a notch, across a snowfield, then the Finger Traverse (a downsloping ledge with a horizontal finger crack and old pitons), or the lower Terrible Traverse, the steep exposed snow crossing above a large cliff, when conditions allow.

patches.fact: Which traverse the North Chute line crosses
patches.find: this chute delivers you toward the TERRIBLE TRAVERSE, a steep exposed snow crossing directly above a large cliff at roughly 7,435 ft, reached after the line loses a little height and traverses north on ledges. If you top out on a notch with a tower just to its left and then find a saddle, a 150 ft drop and a ledge with a horizontal finger crack, you have found the South Chute and the Finger Traverse instead.
patches.replace: near its top the chute narrows and eases, the summit block comes into sight to the north, and a narrow exposed ledge trending left meets the point where the South Chute's gully joins from below. Above that the line is shared with the standard route and crosses the Finger Traverse, or the Terrible Traverse when conditions allow.
